--- title: "If so, how far?" --- The glide that follows from the built glider's own trim, set against the design's, from the same release height. ::: {.callout-tip} ## Specified **All-up mass 16 g, balance point 15 mm aft of the plan's** · measured on the built glider by the user, 2026-08-30. **Release height 1.5 m** · as for the design, so the two are comparable. ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed Still air, and a glide already settled at trim. More seriously, the built glider's trim lies past the stall, where `AeroBuildup` is reading NeuralFoil beyond the attached-flow regime it represents well. The range below is what the model says, not what the model can support. ::: ::: {#9e583b72 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} H, BUILT_M, SHIFT = 1.5, 0.016, 0.015 x_np = neutral_point() x_cg_plan = x_np - 0.10 * c_w plan = trim(0.01550, x_cg_plan) built = trim(BUILT_M, x_cg_built := x_cg_plan + SHIFT) a_stall, _ = stall(built["V"]) ``` ::: **Answer.** The model says 6\.7 m, against 8\.4 m for the design — a glide ratio of 4\.45 where the plan gives 5\.57, so about 20% less distance for the same release. It also comes down faster, sinking 0\.82 m/s against 0\.70, so it is airborne 1\.8 s instead of 2\.1. **Do not trust that number.** It is computed at 10\.0°, and the wing stalls at 9\.7°, so the aircraft is trimmed past the point where the flow stays attached. The section data behind it is a smooth NACA approximation to a flat plate, which is optimistic before the stall and unreliable after it. Read 6\.7 m as an upper bound on a flight that will really be a nose-high mush, and expect a real glider to land nearer the thrower than that — with the direction it lands in largely decided by which wing drops first. The useful comparison is not the two distances but their cause: the design flies 1\.9° below the stall and the article flies past it. Recovering the distance is not a matter of trimming for range; it is a matter of moving the balance point forward until the aircraft is flying on the right side of its own polar again. ::: {#tbl-range .cell tbl-cap='Glide from a 1.5 m release, each at its own trim. The built column is quoted for completeness, not for confidence.' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "": ["trims at", "trim speed", "lift coefficient", "glide ratio", "sink rate", "range from 1.5 m", "time aloft"], "as planned": [f"{plan['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{plan['V']:.2f} m/s", f"{plan['CL']:.3f}", f"{plan['LD']:.2f} : 1", f"{plan['sink']:.2f} m/s", f"{plan['LD']*H:.1f} m", f"{H/plan['sink']:.1f} s"], "as built": [f"{built['alpha']:.1f}°", f"{built['V']:.2f} m/s", f"{built['CL']:.3f}", f"{built['LD']:.2f} : 1", f"{built['sink']:.2f} m/s", f"{built['LD']*H:.1f} m", f"{H/built['sink']:.1f} s"], }).style.hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def trim(mass, x_cg, V=5.0, alpha=None, iters=60): """ The angle of attack and speed at which an aircraft of this mass and balance flies itself: pitching moment about the CG zero, lift equal to weight. Takes mass and CG rather than a MassProperties, so it works for a glider that has been built and weighed as readily as for one that has been summed. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, so it is shifted to the CG first: Cm_cg = Cm_ref + CL * (x_cg - x_ref) / c_ref. Iterated rather than solved, because CL and V each determine the other and the speed moves the polar through Reynolds number. `slope` is dCm/dalpha at the crossing -- negative is a restoring moment. That is the honest stability test: it needs no neutral point, so it does not inherit the ambiguity in defining one. """ a = np.linspace(-2, 14, 161) if alpha is None else alpha for _ in range(iters): p = polars(a, V=V) Cm_cg = np.array(p["Cm"]) + np.array(p["CL"]) * (x_cg - x_qc_w) / c_w i = int(np.argmin(abs(Cm_cg))) V = (2 * mass * 9.81 / (1.225 * S_w * float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]))) ** 0.5 CL, CD = float(np.array(p["CL"])[i]), float(np.array(p["CD"])[i]) return dict(alpha=a[i], V=V, CL=CL, CD=CD, LD=CL / CD, slope=(Cm_cg[i + 1] - Cm_cg[i - 1]) / (a[i + 1] - a[i - 1]), Re=p["Re_c"], sink=V / (1 + (CL / CD) ** 2) ** 0.5) ``` :::
